title: Selection Structures
bullets: If statements allows your program to choose some code to run while not running other code.

title: Selection Structures
paragraphs: A selection structure allows a program to choose between different paths of code.
Instead of always running every line in order, the program checks a condition and decides what should happen next.
In Python, selection structures are commonly created using if, elif, and else.

title: Conditions
paragraphs: A condition is an expression that evaluates to either True or False.
Selection structures use conditions to decide whether a block of code should run.
Comparisons such as 5 > 3 create conditions because Python can determine whether they are true or false.

title: Comparison Operators
paragraphs: Comparison operators compare two values and produce either True or False.
They are commonly used to create conditions inside selection structures.
Python includes operators for equality, inequality, greater than, less than, and combinations of those comparisons.

title: Negating Conditions
paragraphs: Negation reverses the result of a condition.
Python uses the not keyword to change True to False and False to True.
This is useful when you want to check that something is not true.

title: if Statements
paragraphs: An if statement runs a block of code only when its condition evaluates to True.
If the condition is False, that block is skipped.
In Python, the indented lines underneath the if statement belong to its code block.
code:
temperature = 25

if temperature > 20:
    print("It is warm outside.")

print("Program complete.")
expectedOutput:
It is warm outside.
Program complete.
initialOutput:
It is warm outside.
Program complete.

title: else Statements
paragraphs: An else statement provides a fallback when the conditions before it are False.
An else statement does not have its own condition.
It handles any remaining case that was not matched earlier.

title: elif Statements
paragraphs: An elif statement (sometimes called else if statements in other programming languages) checks an additional condition when the conditions before it were False.
Python checks an if / elif structure from top to bottom and runs the first code block whose condition is True.
Once a match is found, the remaining elif and else statements are skipped.

title: Ordering elif Conditions
paragraphs: When several conditions overlap, their order matters because Python stops at the first condition that is True.
For conditions such as score >= 80, score >= 65, and score >= 50, the most restrictive condition should come first and the broadest condition should come last.
A score of 95 satisfies all three conditions, so if score >= 50 appears first, Python will stop there and never reach the more specific checks.

title: Ordering elif Conditions continued...
paragraphs: The first condition, score >= 50, is already True, so Python immediately runs that block and skips the rest.
Even though score >= 80 is also True, Python never reaches it.
For overlapping inequality conditions, order them from most specific to broadest.

title: Wrap Up
bullets: Selection structures allow programs to make decisions by evaluating conditions as True or False.
if checks the first condition, elif allows additional conditions to be checked, and else handles any remaining case.
Comparison operators create many common conditions, while not can reverse a condition.
Because Python checks an if / elif structure from top to bottom, overlapping conditions must be ordered carefully.
